source: manual web-research pass: expert analysis (ESPN, CBS Sports, FantasyPros, RotoBaller, PFF, Footballguys, Yahoo, PhillyVoice, NFL.com) + community consensus, Aug 2026 preseason
disclaimer: Advisory only. Never used in scoring/VORP/ranking math or reason-code generation. Purely supplementary color for the human drafter — cross-reference against players.json projections, which remain the source of truth.

themes.summary: Elite RB tier (Gibbs, Bijan, Taylor, CMC) still viewed as top of the format; RB hit-rate for top-24 finish remains under ~25% historically, so depth bets on mid-round backs are inherently risky.

Multiple experts flag age/mileage risk on veteran workhorse RBs entering 2026 (CMC turns 30, has missed significant time 3 of last 6 years despite huge per-game upside when healthy; Barkley enters year 9 at 29 with 828 touches over prior two seasons; Derrick Henry also in this bucket at his age).

Dual-threat QBs with rushing volume graded as having a higher fantasy floor/ceiling combo this year (Josh Allen's rushing production cited specifically); some analysts see Kyler Murray as a top-6 QB upside play in a low-end QB2 draft slot.

First-round rookie WRs are hitting WR2-or-better as rookies more often than in past cycles; target share/scheme fit and QB quality are the differentiators experts cite for 2026's rookie WR class (Carnell Tate, Makai Lemon among names mentioned).

Recurring theme across sources: rounds ~6-12 are where fantasy teams separate from the pack — backfield committee bets and rookie-role bets in that range are the highest-leverage picks after the top tiers are gone.
